chunks: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who is behind the Imam, and the Imam prolongs the tashahhud. He said: “He may give the taslīm and go on to his need, if he wishes.”

key_terms.أَحَبَّ: he wishes; showing permissibility based on choice
key_terms.إِنْ: if; indicating that the action is optional
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind; indicating his position behind the Imam in congregational prayer
key_terms.لِحَاجَتِهِ: for his need; for some necessity or matter he wishes to attend to
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the taslim; he concludes with the salutation of peace
key_terms.ٱلتَّشَهُّدَ: the tashahhud; the sitting testimony in salat
key_terms.ٱلرَّجُلِ: the man; the person being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the Imam; the one leading the congregational salat

ai.seo_question: Can a person praying behind the Imam give taslim and leave if the Imam prolongs the tashahhud?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one praying behind the Imam when the Imam prolongs the tashahhud. It states that the follower may perform the taslim and leave for his need if he wishes, indicating permissibility in such a situation.
